global_read: state/global.json (fetched 2026-09-01 08:46, unchanged for this 17:00 checkpoint) shows the oil-shock tape holding: Brent 92.15 (+1.83% 1d, +10.0% 1mo) and WTI 87.50 (+2.03% 1d, +8.91% 1mo) after the US-Iran Strait of Hormuz escalation, with VIX 15.55 (+4.22% 1d, still a low absolute level, not panic) and a soft S&P (-0.58% 1d) / Dow (-0.72% 1d) showing global risk appetite cautious in sympathy. Gold +9.66% 1mo keeps a safe-haven bid. USD/PKR (277.29) and DXY (99.62) remain essentially flat -- the FX channel still hasn't cracked, a genuine near-term positive, but it now sits alongside a domestic inflation shock (see drivers) rather than in isolation. Net: global tape is mild-but-real risk-off, and today's domestic CPI print reinforces rather than offsets it.
drivers: Pakistan's August 2026 headline CPI printed 11.1% YoY, sharply up from July's 9.2% and more than triple August 2025's 3.56% -- urban inflation rose to 10.4% (from 8.7%), rural to 12.2% (from 9.9%), MoM inflation +1.2%; this is well above the 5-7% target band SBP itself guided to at the July 27 MPC, and it is a fresh, confirmed domestic upside inflation shock landing on top of the oil-driven external shock, not just a forecast risk anymore -- verified this run via https://propakistani.pk/2026/09/01/inflation-more-than-triples-in-one-year/ and https://www.bolnews.com/pakistan/pakistans-inflation-rises-to-11-15-in-august-2026/

SBP held the policy rate at 11.5% at its last MPC (2026-07-27), its first meeting of FY27; next decision 2026-09-14 -- re-verified this run via https://tribune.com.pk/story/2620561/sbp-keeps-policy-rate-unchanged-at-115-1 . With CPI now printing 11.1% against SBP's own 5-7% end-FY guidance, any near-term rate-cut expectation for the Sept 14 MPC is effectively off the table; the debate now leans toward an extended hawkish hold, with a hike no longer a fringe scenario given oil is a fresh upside risk on top of this print.

SBP-held FX reserves last printed $17,098.5mn (~$17.10bn) for the week ended 2026-08-21 (+$17mn WoW), total liquid reserves ~$22.6bn; no fresher weekly print exists yet as of this 17:00 checkpoint (SBP's next weekly release, for the week ended Aug 28, was not yet out) -- re-verified this run via https://www.brecorder.com/news/40435778/sbp-held-forex-reserves-rise-by-25mn-to-1708bn . A reserve buffer this thin (~2.6 months import cover) has little room to absorb a sustained oil-driven import-bill increase without PKR or reserve stress.

IMF's 4th EFF / 3rd RSF review mission remains reported for the second week of September 2026 (schedule still not finalized); Pakistan is reported on track to meet 6 of 7 quantitative performance criteria, with ~$1.2bn combined disbursement (~$1bn EFF + ~$200mn RSF) at stake; energy-sector circular debt remains the key sticking point, and the mission is also expected to scrutinize Sovereign Wealth Fund law amendments and the Governance and Anti-Corruption Diagnostics reform plan -- re-verified this run via https://propakistani.pk/2026/08/28/pakistan-imf-to-begin-4th-review-of-7-billion-eff-in-september/ and https://dailytimes.com.pk/1545032/imf-mission-expected-in-pakistan-next-month-for-loan-programme-reviews/

T-bill/PIB carry remains elevated and was already grinding up auction-over-auction before both this week's oil shock and today's CPI print: last MTB round (2026-08-20) cut off at 1M 11.47%, 3M 11.65%, 6M 11.80%, 12M 11.99%; last PIB round (2026-08-05) at 3Y 11.745%, 5Y 11.80%, 10Y 12.30%, 15Y 12.485%. No fresher auction this run -- verified via https://tribune.com.pk/story/2624826/govt-raises-rs498b-via-t-bills-as-yields-rise . With CPI now confirmed at 11.1%, the next round is more likely to price a further premium than any relief.
